title: 龟虽寿
author: 曹操
intro: Written by a warlord in his fifties, this short poem admits that even a magic tortoise must die — then refuses to give up: an old warhorse in its stall still dreams of galloping a thousand miles.
analysis: 这首诗是曹操五十多岁时写的，谈的是一个很大的问题：人老了、终究要死，那该怎么活？前四句先承认事实：传说中能活几千年的神龟，也有死的时候；能腾云驾雾的神蛇，最后也化成土灰。连神物都逃不过，何况人。接下来笔锋一转，用一个比喻说出全诗最有名的话：“老骥伏枥，志在千里”——一匹老了的千里马趴在马槽边，心里想的还是奔跑千里。“烈士暮年，壮心不已”，有抱负的人到了晚年，雄心也不会停止。“烈士”在这里不是今天“为国牺牲的人”的意思，而是“有远大志向的人”。后面四句又讲道理：寿命长短不全由老天决定，保养好身心，也能活得长久。全诗先抑后扬，既清醒又乐观，没有一点悲观叹老的味道。“老骥伏枥”后来成了成语，常用来形容老当益壮。
analysisEn: Cao Cao wrote this in his fifties, and it faces a big question head-on: we all grow old and die, so how should we live? The first four lines simply accept the facts. The legendary tortoise that lives thousands of years still dies one day; the flying serpent that rides the mist ends up as dust. If even magical creatures can’t escape, people certainly can’t. Then the poem turns, with its most famous image: an old thoroughbred lies by its feeding trough, yet its heart is still set on running a thousand li. In the same way, a man of ambition keeps his drive even late in life. Note that 烈士 here means “a man of high ambition”, not its modern sense of “martyr”. The next lines argue that how long we live is not decided by Heaven alone — looking after body and mind can earn us more years. The poem moves from a sober admission to a confident lift, with no self-pity at all. 老骥伏枥 is still a common idiom today for someone old in years but young in spirit.
background: Cao Cao (155–220) was the most powerful warlord at the end of the Han dynasty and laid the foundations of the state of Wei; he was also a leading poet. This is the last of four sections of his suite “Walking Out of Xiamen Gate” (步出夏门行), traditionally dated to 207, after his victorious campaign against the Wuhuan in the north, when he was 53.
pronunciation: 老骥 jì（千里马）；伏枥 lì（马槽）；腾蛇也写作“螣蛇”，读 téng；盈缩之期 qī；终为土灰 wéi。
version: 采用统编教材（八年级上册）文本。本诗是曹操乐府《步出夏门行》四章中的最后一章，全章十四句（四言），网站按两句一行排版。“腾蛇”一作“螣蛇”。

lines.py: shén guī suī shòu, yóu yǒu jìng shí
lines.lit: Though the divine tortoise lives long, there is still a time when it ends.
lines.en: The sacred tortoise lives for ages, yet its days, too, run out.

lines.py: téng shé chéng wù, zhōng wéi tǔ huī
lines.lit: The soaring serpent rides the mist, but finally becomes earth and ash.
lines.en: The flying serpent rides the mist, and still it comes to dust.

lines.py: lǎo jì fú lì, zhì zài qiān lǐ
lines.lit: The old thoroughbred lies by the trough; its will is set on a thousand li.
lines.en: An old warhorse rests at its manger, its heart still racing a thousand miles.

lines.py: liè shì mù nián, zhuàng xīn bù yǐ
lines.lit: A man of ambition in his late years — his bold heart does not stop.
lines.en: A man of spirit in his evening years never lets his great heart rest.

lines.py: yíng suō zhī qī, bù dàn zài tiān
lines.lit: The span of growing and shrinking is not decided only by Heaven;
lines.en: How long or short our lives may be is not up to Heaven alone;

lines.py: yǎng yí zhī fú, kě dé yǒng nián
lines.lit: With the blessing of nourishing a calm mind, one can gain long years.
lines.en: keep body and mind at peace, and you may win many years.

lines.py: xìng shèn zhì zāi, gē yǐ yǒng zhì
lines.lit: How very fortunate! I sing to express my aims.
lines.en: What joy this is! So I sing it out, to tell what my heart is set on.

words.en: divine tortoise (said to live thousands of years)
words.note: 古人认为龟能活很久，是长寿的象征。
古义“终了”，今天还在“未竟的事业”里用；现代汉语常用义是“竟然”。
传说中能乘云雾飞行的蛇。

words.en: in the end becomes dust and ash
a fine horse that can run a thousand li
words.note: 现代汉语一般说“千里马”。

words.en: to lie by the feeding trough
words.note: 枥：马槽。“老骥伏枥”今天是成语，形容人老了仍有雄心。
古义；今天“烈士”指为国家、为正义牺牲的人，意思很不一样。

words.en: old age; the evening of life
words.note: 暮：傍晚。现代书面语仍用。
已：停止。现代汉语有“激动不已”“赞叹不已”。

words.en: growing and shrinking — i.e. how long or short a life is
words.note: 盈：满；缩：亏。这里指寿命长短。

words.en: to nourish body and keep the mind cheerful
words.note: 怡：愉快。现代汉语有“心旷神怡”。

words.py: xìng shèn zhì zāi, gē yǐ yǒng zhì
words.en: how fortunate! I sing to voice my aims
words.note: 乐府演唱时加在每章末尾的套语，和正文意思关系不大。

imagery.name: 马
imagery.zh: 老骥是诗人自比：身体老了，奔驰千里的志向还在。
imagery.en: The old thoroughbred is the poet himself: the body is aging, but the urge to gallop a thousand li is still there.
